name: next-alarm-to-workstation
description: Push the time the next alarm rings to the workstation each time it changes, so a tray icon there can show it without polling the phone. next_alarm_changed rides the system's own next-alarm broadcast, which fires whenever any alarm is created, edited, switched on or off, deleted, snoozed, or dismissed in a way that moves the soonest one, so the only added cost is one short SSH connection per change. It also fires once when the engine starts and on each Wi-Fi join, which is what puts the current value on the tray the moment the phone arrives home. Home is proved the way the other home rules prove it: the DHCP lease has to match and the SSH connection with kata's key has to succeed, so nothing is sent from any other network. The connection goes over the Wi-Fi network itself, because on a join the event fires before Wi-Fi is the default route. A lost push is retried only briefly, because the next change supersedes it. The workstation verb is `alarm <epoch ms>`, -1 when no alarm is set; its answer lands in the run record.

params.label: Workstation verb that records the next alarm
